statement.text:
Can the question 7.28 on conditions for admissibility of an elementary carpet
A = {Ar | r ∈ Φ} be reduced to Lie rank 1 if K is a field? A carpet A of type Φ
of additive subgroups of K is called addmissible if in the Chevalley group over K
associated with the root system Φ the subgroup ⟨xr (Ar ) | r ∈ Φ⟩ intersects xr (K) in
xr (Ar ). More precisely, is it true that the carpet A is admissible if and only if the
subcarpets {Ar , A−r }, r ∈ Φ, of rank 1 are admissible? The answer is known to be
affirmative if the field K is locally finite (V. M. Levchuk, Algebra and Logic, 22, no. 5
(1983), 362–371).                                                         V. M. Levchuk
